mentl/5b4de07:
The cached-cursor mode is cross-run real. Patch one module of a DAG and
the next compile restores the image, names the exact cone (warm:
re-deriving b main — a stays cached), re-judges only the cone into the
restored world, and re-persists; the emission is byte-identical to a
cold compile of the patched tree, and a third run answers image current
— nothing re-derived.

The image carries its own manifest, entry name, and per-module statement
buckets as typed roots, so the post-swap path takes zero pre-swap heap
arguments; the current tree reads fresh off the host fs. Re-registration
shadows stale entries and the entry is always in a nonempty cone — every
DAG module is one of its transitive deps.

The eight interrogations cut the build twice before it landed: warm_root
was a stored flatten of warm_asts — the derived value persisted beside
its source — and died into the warm_program projection; and the pairs,
deps, and order walks were three content passes over the same files,
fused into one driver_tree_scan whose consumers are projections. Two
catalog classes fired live on the way. The pointer-eq class hit twice:
module_in and manifest_hash_of compared erased list elements at the word
floor, so every module changed and none joined the cone — the empty
re-deriving line was the tell; the String pins carry the proof until
name-is-handle retires str_eq. And E_DuplicateFnName decoupled from the
env into the registration walk's own seen-set: an env-based check
misreads a prior judgment's entry as a duplicate the moment the cone
re-registers — the exact flaw the two-pass build named, its banked
design now the landed form with the incremental cursor as first
consumer.

Every WABT tool needs --enable-tail-call --enable-threads or it chokes on opcode
0x13 (return_call_indirect) — which is why wasm-objdump/wat2wasm are the workhorses
and wasm-stats/wasm2wat sat unused. With the flags ALL work on m2: objdump -h gives
the Code-section SIZE baseline (≈1.18MB/2532fn) — a runaway-emit shows as a fat Code
delta (the LFnRef Part-A bloat hit 3x); wasm-stats gives the opcode distribution;
wasm2wat --fold-exprs gives readable WAT (never grep the raw 12MB m2.wat). The
binary-arbitration that powers the proven pipeline IS this toolkit used fully.

celezdial/5bfe57f:
Chrome on large desktop displays was freezing the entire laptop when
playing notes; phone was fine because its viewport is ~4× smaller.

Canvas emanation painted radial gradients whose radius scaled with full
canvas height (78-95%) on an unclamped root-sized canvas. On a 1300px-tall
root with 24 active voices, that's ~98 Mpx/frame of radial-gradient
rasterization — past the threshold where Chrome's 2D canvas stalls the
GPU driver and takes the compositor with it.

- Cap canvas intrinsic resolution at 1200px/dim; CSS stretches back to
  100% (glow is soft, upscale invisible). setTransform keeps draw code
  in root CSS-pixel space.
- Cap gradient radius at 3× largest key extent — keeps emanation local
  to each key instead of covering the viewport.
- Lower falloff constants 78/95 → 40/50 as consistent pre-cap defaults.

~18× reduction in worst-case per-frame pixel work.
